The generation model takes (1) context: the concatenation of the piece of text x (of document D) containing the current event trigger and the event type's corresponding template in the ontology; (2) memory store m: of previously extracted events of the same document D, as input, and learns a distribution p(y|x, m) over possible outputs y.

We consider an argument span to be correctly identified if its offsets match any of the gold/reference informative arguments ... We also report performance under a more lenient metric 'Coref F1'. ... Precision (P), Recall (R) and F1 scores are reported.

We consider an argument span to be correctly identified if its offsets match any of the gold/reference informative arguments of the current event (i.e., argument identification); and it is correctly classified if its semantic role also matches (i.e., argument classification).
